clue.text: British city's drains

parts.note: Leeds is a large city in Yorkshire, northern England

explanation.surface: A British city's drainage system is under discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drains' reads as a noun in the surface but is the verb in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To drain fluid away and to lose blood or money steadily are the same verb sense, a synonym pair.

clue.text: Show disapproval for two unknown characters inclined to tipple

parts.note: to boo is to show disapproval by jeering
in algebra z and y are standard letters for unknown quantities

explanation.surface: Frowning on two mysterious drinkers who like the bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Fond of alcohol and likely to drink heavily; tipple means to drink habitually.

clue.text: Bodily substance of England's opener and No. 11?

indicators.note: opener means the first letter, punning on a cricket opening batsman

parts.note: the number eleven batsman in cricket is the final one to bat, the last man in

explanation.surface: A cricket question: what substance links England's first and final batsmen?
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the No. 11 is the last batsman in the order.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretchy protein in connective tissue such as skin and arteries, an example of a body substance.

clue.text: Like something studied by vicar travelling in cold train?

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so these letters are shifted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clergyman reads on a chilly railway journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to church teaching or dogma, which a clergyman would study.

clue.text: Geared-up bishop was in marathon maybe

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop
a marathon is one example of a race, so taking part in one means you ran a race

explanation.surface: A clergyman who ran a marathon was well prepared beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: Being prepared or ready for something, as when bracing yourself for impact, is a synonym of geared-up.

clue.text: Accommodation using basic cleaning devices first off

indicators.note: first off means the opening letter of the word is removed

parts.note: brooms are simple sweeping tools

explanation.surface: Lodgings where the simplest cleaning tools come out first.
explanation.definitionFit: Lodgings or rented space are synonyms, as in rooms to let.

clue.text: Paramedic working with journalist rejected drink

indicators.note: working means operating or in action, so the letters of paramedic are put to work in a new order
rejected means thrown out, so the journalist letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: An ambulance worker and a reporter turn down an aperitif.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges PARAMEDIC, and 'rejected' removes ED, leaving CAMPARI.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitter red Italian aperitif, an example of an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Exceptionally deft clue I made up

indicators.note: exceptionally suggests out of the ordinary, so these letters are arranged unusually

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A setter boasts of a brilliantly crafted clue they composed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made up' looks like the setter composing, but it means invented or false.
explanation.definitionFit: Something invented and untrue is dishonest, so fabricated stories are deceptive.

clue.text: After one short day chief becomes king?

parts.note: Mon is the shortened form of Monday, one of the days of the week
arch means chief or principal, as in archbishop or arch-enemy

explanation.surface: After a brief day in charge, the boss is elevated to royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that a monarch need not be a king: a queen is one too.
explanation.definitionFit: A king is one example of a sovereign ruler, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Old maiden in tactile experience gets more than is wanted

indicators.note: the words old maiden are placed in the middle of the tactile experience

parts.note: touch is the sense of feeling something physically
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: An elderly spinster finds physical contact overwhelming.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, abbreviated M.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for an excessive amount describes exactly what is beyond what anyone wanted.

clue.text: One sending on a message supporting prison employee

parts.note: for means in favour of or supporting
a warder is a prison guard

explanation.surface: A prison guard who backs someone passes on a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: One who passes mail or freight onward to another address does this job, a descriptive definition.

clue.text: Puzzle misery to us puzzling

indicators.note: as an imperative, puzzle asks us to confuse these letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A misery that baffles us remains a riddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puzzle' is a verb telling the solver to scramble 'misery to'; 'us' stays put at the end, and the adjective 'puzzling' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Baffling and enigmatic are synonyms, both adjectives for what cannot be explained.

clue.text: Opposing battle without court's backing

indicators.note: without tells us to take the court away from the battle's name

parts.note: Agincourt was the 1415 battle won by Henry V of England in northern France
the word court is the back end of the battle's name, which 'backing' points to

explanation.surface: Someone is against a fight that lacks the support of the law courts.
explanation.walkthrough: Agincourt is the famous English victory over the French in 1415.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect or jocular word meaning against, used of someone who opposes an idea.

clue.text: Yesteryear's Tony enthralling one country

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the politician's name holds the one inside it

parts.note: Tony Benn was a veteran British Labour politician who died in 2014
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A former figure named Tony captivated a particular nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Benn was a long-serving left-wing Labour MP and minister.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a West African nation bordering Nigeria and Togo, an example of a state.

clue.text: Naughty saboteur seen around end of park escapes

indicators.note: around means the rearranged saboteur surrounds the letter from park
naughty means badly behaved, so the letters of saboteur are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: end of means the final letter of the word park

explanation.surface: A mischievous wrecker is spotted near a park's edge, escaping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naughty' rearranges SABOTEUR into BREAOUTS, which goes around K.
explanation.definitionFit: Jailbreaks or escapes from confinement are synonyms, plural noun to plural noun.

clue.text: Theologian takes rock face into river

indicators.note: into means the rock face is inserted inside the river name

parts.note: the Wye is a river flowing along the border of England and Wales
a cliff is a steep rock face

explanation.surface: A scholar of religion pushes a sheer crag into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wye runs between England and Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: John Wycliffe was the fourteenth-century English scholar and reformer who sponsored the first English Bible translation.

clue.text: Force prisoners on to vehicle at station?

indicators.note: in a down clue on to means placed above, so the prisoners come first

parts.note: cons is short for convicts, prisoners
a train is a vehicle that stops at stations

explanation.surface: Convicts are compelled to board a train at the station.
explanation.definitionFit: To compel, restrict or oblige someone is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Sneer about fine shopkeeper with expensive goods?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the sneer goes around the word for fine

parts.note: to jeer is to sneer or mock
well means fine or in good health

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a fine shop owner selling costly items.
explanation.definitionFit: A seller of gems and precious metals runs a shop full of costly items, described here loosely.

clue.text: Survey quarry after fire upset

indicators.note: after means the quarry comes after the upturned fire word
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word for fire is read from the bottom

parts.note: to axe is to fire or sack someone
a mine is a quarry or pit for extraction

explanation.surface: Inspecting a pit after a blaze has caused distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns AXE into EXA.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect or scrutinise something closely is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Chemist illustrious but ultimately a bit twisted

indicators.note: only a small bit at the end of the word for illustrious, its final pair of letters, is turned around

parts.note: noble means illustrious or distinguished

explanation.surface: An eminent scientist turns out to be slightly bent at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately a bit twisted' swaps only the last two letters, giving EL for LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Nobel, Swedish chemist and inventor of dynamite, founded the prizes bearing his name.

clue.text: Someone using vessel to cross lake for fish

indicators.note: to cross means to span or straddle, so the boat user goes around the lake letter

parts.note: a boater is someone who uses a boat

explanation.surface: A sailor crosses a lake looking for fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A cured smoked herring, an example of fish.

clue.text: One sort of bird driving other sorts back

indicators.note: driving back means pushing in reverse, so the other birds are read from the end
back pairs with driving to tell us the word is read in reverse

parts.note: auks are a different family of seabirds, such as puffins and guillemots

explanation.surface: One bird species is chasing away other kinds.
explanation.definitionFit: A predatory seabird of northern oceans, one example of a bird species.

clue.text: Search by one remarkable person who wants an answer?

parts.note: a quest is a search
I is the Roman numeral for one
a oner is British slang for something or someone remarkable, one of a kind

explanation.surface: A searching investigator wants to know the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: ONER is old British slang for an outstanding person or thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone asking things is by nature seeking a reply, a descriptive definition.

clue.text: Sporting venue where cards were played right: Queen, Ace and Jack

definitions.text: Sporting venue where cards were played right

parts.note: Q is the abbreviation for queen, as on playing cards
A is the abbreviation for ace, as on playing cards
jack and tar are both old slang for a sailor

explanation.surface: A card game's royal hand: queen, ace and jack, played at a sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The country hosted the 2022 football World Cup after a controversial bid: it played its cards right.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gulf state hosted the 2022 football World Cup, having successfully won the bidding.

clue.text: Silver forged without letter to indicate Queen or King

indicators.note: forged means hammered into a new shape, so the letters of silver are reshaped
without means the queen letter is left out

parts.note: taken as written
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen, as in ER

explanation.surface: Silver worked into a monogram showing royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: Elvis Presley is known as the King of rock and roll.
explanation.definitionFit: The singer was nicknamed the King of rock and roll, a famous epithet.

clue.text: Daughter is among crazy people who make an exhibition of themselves?

definitions.text: people who make an exhibition of themselves?

indicators.note: among means placed within, so the daughter and is go inside the crazy word

parts.note: nuts means crazy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A daughter is mixing with lunatics who show off in public.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is whimsical: naturists literally expose themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturists who go unclothed literally put their bodies on display, a punning twist on showing off.

clue.text: Prisoner in awful pit, in hollowed- out space

indicators.note: the second in tells us the rearranged pit goes inside the hollow space

parts.note: a cave is a hollowed-out space in rock

indicators.note: awful suggests something messed up, so the letters of pit are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An inmate is held in a dreadful pit within a hollow chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is a link; the second, after 'awful pit', is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone taken and held against their will is a synonym of an inmate or detainee.

clue.text: Go wrong in attempt to provide drink before meal?

indicators.note: in means the going wrong is placed inside the attempt

parts.note: a shy is a try or attempt, as in a coconut shy
to err is to go wrong or make a mistake

explanation.surface: Messing up an attempt to serve an aperitif.
explanation.walkthrough: A coconut shy is a British fairground game of throwing balls, hence shy for a throw or attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified wine often served as an aperitif, an example of a pre-dinner drink.

clue.text: Animal home is beyond road going west

indicators.note: beyond means coming after, so is follows the road

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: in an across clue going west means read from right to left, so the road is backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A creature's home lies past a road heading westward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going west' turns RD into DR.
explanation.definitionFit: The indri is a large lemur of Madagascar, an example of an animal.
